Admissions and Pre-Admission Assessment Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 February 2025. Removes the same-day admission allowance for a
non-emergency case pending the full GP summary, and adds a mandatory documented mental capacity
screen to every pre-admission assessment.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group assesses a prospective resident before admission. It
applies to every admission, whether privately funded or arranged through a local authority or the NHS.

Policy statement

A pre-admission assessment establishes whether Alderbridge can safely and appropriately meet a
prospective resident's needs before they arrive, protecting both the individual and the existing resident
community from an admission the service is not equipped to support.

Definitions

**Pre-admission assessment** the structured assessment of a prospective resident's needs, completed
before an admission is agreed, now including a mandatory mental capacity screen. **GP summary** the
prospective resident's medical summary from their current GP, now required before a non-emergency
admission proceeds. **Emergency placement** a genuinely urgent admission meeting the defined
emergency criteria, the only route under this version where admission may proceed ahead of the full
written GP summary.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager or a deputy** completes the pre-admission assessment, including a
home-manager phone call with the prospective resident's current GP and the new mandatory mental
capacity screen. **The admissions coordinator** gathers supporting information, including the GP
summary, ahead of the assessment visit, and now confirms the full summary has been received before a
non-emergency admission is scheduled. **The multidisciplinary team**, where involved, contributes
specialist input for a prospective resident with complex needs.

1. Complete a face-to-face pre-admission assessment before agreeing any non-emergency admission,
covering care needs, risk, and compatibility with the site's current resident group.

1. Complete a face-to-face pre-admission assessment before agreeing any non-emergency admission,
covering care needs, risk, and compatibility with the site's current resident group.

3. Make a home-manager phone call to the prospective resident's current GP as part of the assessment,

5. Only an admission meeting the defined emergency placement criteria may proceed ahead of the full
written GP summary, with the summary followed up and reviewed within 72 hours.

6. Confirm the site can meet the prospective resident's specific needs, including any specialist equipment
or staffing ratio required, before admission is agreed.

before the resident's first day.

Involving family in the assessment visit

Where a prospective resident wishes for family to be present during the assessment visit, this is
accommodated wherever practicable, since family input often surfaces relevant history or preference the
prospective resident themselves may not think to mention, without the family's presence replacing a direct
conversation with the prospective resident wherever they are able to take part in one.

Assessing compatibility with the existing resident group

The assessment also considers how a prospective resident's needs and personality are likely to fit with the
site's existing resident group, since a poor compatibility fit can affect both the new resident's own
settling-in experience and the wellbeing of residents already living there, and this consideration sits
alongside, not instead of, the clinical, capacity-screen and care-needs elements of the assessment.

Closing note

A thorough pre-admission assessment protects a prospective resident from an admission that will not
meet their needs as much as it protects the service, and the changes in this version exist to close two
specific gaps identified in practice without making the process unworkable for a genuine emergency.

requiring the summary first, except in a genuine emergency, closes that gap. **What does the new mental
capacity screen actually assess?** It is an initial, structured check of whether the prospective resident
appears to have capacity relevant to their admission and care decisions, feeding into but not replacing any
fuller capacity assessment needed later.

Training and competency

Registered managers and deputies complete pre-admission assessment training, refreshed every two
years, updated to cover the mental capacity screen and the narrowed emergency placement route.

Monitoring and compliance

Completed assessments and admission outcomes are reviewed monthly by the Quality Lead, including
specific attention to emergency placement route usage and mental capacity screen completion rates.

Record keeping and retention

Pre-admission assessments, including the mental capacity screen outcome, are retained in the resident's
care record per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This policy was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 1 February 2025 and this version took effect
1 February 2026, superseding the earlier version.
